column1: # tests/selection/matrix.tsv - L2 of the change->test dependency matrix.
# Globs are bash 3.2 `case` patterns: `*` crosses `/`, `**` is a synonym for `*`,
# alternation is `|`, braces are FORBIDDEN (case does not expand them).
# Targets are comma-separated paths under tests/shell/ without the .bats suffix,
# or the sole literal NONE (reviewed: ALWAYS set only) or FULL.
# Rows are a UNION - every matching row contributes. The rationale column is
# mandatory: dropping coverage must cost a reviewed diff, never a silent omission.
# --- L2 headline: the repo-wide doc checkers --------------------------------

column4: section-lint and desc-lint both run repo-wide over agents/, commands/ and skills/; cross-plugin-refs, test-authority-matrix and skill-refs scan every agent doc. skill-refs reads each agent's tools: line against the Skill calls and plugin paths in its body.
Same five repo-wide checkers as R01; command docs are inside their scan roots, and skill-refs resolves the Skill targets they name.
Same four repo-wide checkers. `*` crosses `/`, so this covers SKILL.md and references/**.md at any depth.

column1: # --- per-agent specialisations, derived from hooks that hardcode an agent ----

column4: All four hooks hardcode corpflow:developer; M6 re-derives this edge from the hook sources so it cannot rot. dv-tree-preflight is added by hand: the script exists to serve developer.md D0.0, and that gate is specified in the agent doc rather than in the script.
Named in dv-screenshot-gate.sh as an agent_type and in test-execution-gate.sh where QA's full-run authority is decided.
dv-comment-density-gate.sh names technical-lead as a reviewing role in its exemption reasoning.
These three are the only agents whose frontmatter wires the Stop hook to hooks/agent-stop.sh.
Reviewed: no hook hardcodes these names and no parity source reads them, so R01's four repo-wide checkers plus ALWAYS are the correct and complete answer.
The megatask command doc is the contract these three drive; none of them spells its path, so L1 cannot see the edge.

Branch naming, branch refinement and the Step 2a duplicate-issue pre-flight gate are specified in the worktask command doc rather than in the scripts themselves; the § Phase 0 --resume entry point is likewise specified here rather than in state-patch.sh, so an edit to it must select the --task-replay tests.
The self-improvement pipeline stages are sequenced by this command doc, not by any path either script names.

column1: # --- shared docs: only where a doc governs an executable contract -----------

column4: The authority matrix and the execution gate both implement the stage test authority this doc defines.
Branch and commit naming rules here are the specification the first three scripts encode; § Pull Request Format specifies the body shape adhoc-visual-evidence splices into and pr-body-lint checks.

The absolute-path strip rule lives in publish-pl-issue-lib.sh and is duplicated in pr-body-lint.sh; the entrypoint, its sanitiser library and its self-test harness are one unit, and fn-preflight, attach-visual-evidence and the cross-plugin registry parity all read that library.
Stage codes and artifact names are the shared vocabulary of the ledger, the artifact map and both preflight hooks.
Task status vocabulary and ledger transitions are what state-patch writes and state-merge reconciles.
The cross-plugin reference checker validates invocation ids against this registry.
The routing-matrix contract test validates alias shape and every mandated inline copy against this file; cross-plugin-refs resolves its default targets against sibling checkouts.

Reviewed: these twelve are high-fanout prose with no executable contract behind them, so R03 plus ALWAYS is correct. Enumerated one by one so the silence is reviewed rather than accidental; M5 asserts the enumeration stays complete.
tests/fixtures/README.md partitions fixtures by owning track; the worktask fixtures are the shared read surface for every worktask/*.bats.
Same partition, skills track. Split out of R18 because a target column is static and the three fixture groups have disjoint consumers.
Same partition, hooks track: stdin payload fixtures are shared across every hook test.
Reviewed: the fixture index is prose about write-access partitioning; no test parses it, so ALWAYS is the correct answer.
Several hook tests assert their own event and matcher wiring against the manifest; only four of the eleven spell its path, so L1 sees a minority of the real edges.
The canvas end-to-end guard drives this fixture tree directly.
